ops-oncall: 🔔 alert — apiserver watch backoff spike in eu-west2-edge, lots of pending watch requeues and 503s, noticed ~2:20 UTC
ops-oncall: graphs: https://grafana.internal/redwood/apiserver-watches?orgId=1&from=now-15m to=now
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (apiserver-watch-backoff-eu-west2-edge) — priority P1
alex: seeing high etcd disk wait on the leader nodes in that region, iops jump ~5x at same time window
maria: node list: controlplane-{a,b,c}-eu2 are leader candidates, pvc metrics show burst write latency 40-60ms
jin: also correlates with a large GPU cluster rollout in eu-west2-edge starting at 02:10 — many pods scheduling, controllers reconciling
kai: could be controller-manager hotlooping on failed pod bindings, flood of events -> watch churn
alex: run this to check event backlog on leader: ```kubectl --context=eu2 get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50```
alex: log excerpt: ```E0402 02:22:15.123 controller.go:215] error syncing 'gpu-pool-xyz': failed to bind: timed out waiting for device allocation```
maria: apiserver logs show repeated "watch: backoff" and "upgrade: broken pipe" entries, here's a sample: ```2026-04-02T02:23:01Z apiserver watch: backoff 120s, caused by EOF```
jin: I'm seeing autoscaler spikes in the GPU autoscaler controller, it keeps creating pods then failing -> lots of object churn
kai: any network egress issues? last week we had an edge egress policy causing pod image pulls to stall in that zone
ops-oncall: no obvious cloud egress alerts but checking firewall logs now, pulling VPC flow logs for eu-west2-edge
eng-release: FYI we had a scheduled rolling update to the gpu-runtime image at 02:05 in that region (canary -> all)
alex: that matches — image pull surge combined with controller requeues caused etcd write bursts (lease/grant churn). IOPS pressure -> apiserver timeouts -> clients backoff
maria: mitigation idea: throttle rollout, pause kube-controller-manager and GPU autoscaler in region for 10m to let etcd and apiserver recover
jin: agree. I'll scale down the rollout replicaset and pause the rollout job. Jake (on release) can you pause the release? @eng-release
eng-release: pausing rollout now, stopping batch deploy job on eu-west2-edge (confirmed) :white_check_mark:
ops-oncall: pausing controllers: ```kubectl --context=eu2 -n kube-system scale deploy kube-controller-manager --replicas=0``` — will also annotate for manual resume
kai: we should also bump etcd disk iops on the three leaders if pause doesn't drop latency in 5m. Opened cloud ticket to increase iops for the rg
alex: snapshotting current etcd metrics and taking a manual backup before any scaling: ```ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap-2260001122.db --endpoints=https://10.0.0.1:2379```
maria: apiserver 95p latency down from 4.2s -> 1.1s after pause of rollout and controller scale-down (2:30 UTC) :thumbsup:
jin: requeue rate dropped by 80%, event backlog draining, no new OOMs or binding errors in logs as of 02:33
ops-oncall: cloud ticket created INC-CLD-789 to bump iops if we see another surge; keep watchers on till 03:00 UTC
eng-release: we'll revert the rollout to canary and re-run with rate limits on controller for image pulls and backoff jitter next time
alex: follow-up actions: 1) add autoscaler rate limiter, 2) pre-warm etcd if large rollout planned (warm leases), 3) add alert for watch-backoffs (SLO)
